title: Pin resolution provenance & routing decision playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
- Capture an operational playbook for how the control plane should resolve model version pins, record provenance for that decision, and translate pins into routing/fallback behavior across regions and capacity tiers.
- Focus: decision logic, metadata to persist for audits, telemetry hooks, and concrete examples for common edge cases.

Background / Problem statement:
- Customers can pin routes to model versions (model:vX) in the registry and also rely on routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity). When capacity constraints or incompatibilities occur we need clear, deterministic behavior.
- Today: ad-hoc behaviors implemented in multiple places; debugging is hard because we lack a single provenance record for how the final serving model was chosen.

Goals:
- Deterministic and explainable pin-resolution algorithm with minimal tail-latency impact.
- Persist a compact provenance record per request and per rollout to aid audits and regression investigations.
- Ensure safe fallbacks across region/capacity tiers while honoring customer pins as much as possible.
- Surface routing policy interactions in the Console/Logs for runbooks and SRE.

Non-goals:
- Not redesigning the entire registry data model here. This is an operations and control-plane playbook.

Key concepts and definitions (informal):
- Pin: user-declared mapping modelName -> modelVersion (could be semantic like stable, canary, exact tag).
- Resolution: process that maps a pin + caller context + routing policy -> concrete artifact (binary build id / config).
- Provenance record: immutable structured string we persist to the request trace containing the inputs and the decision path.
- Compatibility flag: binary tag set at model onboarding and build-time indicating feature-contracts (e.g., kv-cache-layout=v2, tokenizer=sp10).

Decision flow (high level):
1) Ingress: request arrives with route metadata (customer id, route config, explicit pin if present).
2) Local cache lookup: check control-plane cache for recent resolution for (route,pin,region,policy_snapshot). If hit and cache still valid -> return.
3) Fetch registry record: if cache miss, query registry (primary read replica nearest region) for pin target and compatibility labels.
4) Policy evaluation: evaluate routing policy tiers in order (pinned->local-affinity->latency-tier->cost-tier->cross-region-fallback). Each tier yields candidate set.
5) Compatibility filter: remove candidates incompatible with required compatibility flags from route config or request headers.
6) Capacity check: ask capacity service for warm/available candidates. If none available in same region: escalate to cross-region or lower-tier variants.
7) Final tie-breaker: deterministic sort (semantic version desc, build timestamp desc, availability score).
8) Persist provenance: write a single-line provenance blob to the registry audit stream and attach digest to request trace.

Provenance blob schema (stringified key=value pairs; keep flat):
- ts=YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ | route=R | customer=C | pin=model:ver | policy=policy-id | candidates=comma-separated-ids | compat-filter=reason | capacity-filter=reason | selected=id | fallback-path=ordered-steps | resolv-src=cache|registry|manual | traceId=xxxx
Example: 
- ts=20250209T154213Z | route=payments/summary | customer=acme | pin=gpt-remix:3.2.1 | policy=latency-pref-1 | candidates=a12,b34,c56 | compat-filter=removed(b34:kv-v1) | capacity-filter=removed(a12:region-full) | selected=c56 | fallback-path=pin->region->tier | resolv-src=registry | traceId=abc-123

Compatibility matrix approach (operational):
- We do not attempt a full NxN matrix in the control plane for every model pair. Instead:
  - At onboarding time, compute and store a compact capability-set for each build (string tags).
  - Runtime compatibility is evaluated via tag intersections and a small set of policy rules (allow/deny lists).
  - For critical breaking changes (tokenizer, kv-layout), a one-time cross-check job runs to populate a precomputed "hard-incompat" index used by the resolver.

Routing fallback modes (ordered):
- honor-pin-strict: fail fast (400) if pinned version unavailable or incompatible.
- honor-pin-soft: try pinned version; if unavailable after Xs, fallback to compatible variant in same region. Record fallback.
- prefer-pin-but-fallback: only used for canary/auto-rollouts where we prefer pinned but allow controlled fallback to stable.
- ignore-pin: route by policy (used for some internal system routes).

Default for customer routes: honor-pin-soft (with conservative timeout). Enterprise config may set honor-pin-strict.

Telemetry/Observability requirements:
- Metric: pin_resolution_latency_ms (histogram) by route, pin-mode.
- Count: pin_fallbacks_total by reason (compatibility, capacity, policy).
- Trace annotation: attach provenance blob digest and mapping to full blob stored in audit-log bucket.
- Log: when a fallback occurs, emit human-readable line with route, pin, selected, reason (write to routes.fallbacks stream).
- Dashboard: per-customer pin_fallback_rate with drill-down to version pairs causing most fallbacks.

Examples / worked scenarios:
1) Canary -> stable fallback (same region):
   - Customer pins route to model:canary-2025-02-01. Canary has new kv-layout (kv-v2). Stable is model:stable with kv-v1.
   - Request arrives, compatibility filter removes stable; canary capacity is saturated. honor-pin-soft -> no compatible variants => fallback blocked. Return 503 with clear error: "pinned model incompatible with available variants".
2) Pinned exact but region outage:
   - Pin: model:2.1.0, region:us-east-1 preference. Region outage, model available in eu-west-1. honor-pin-soft -> cross-region fallback allowed -> select eu-west variant, add latency-warning header and record fallback.
3) Rolling pin upgrade with tolerant policy:
   - Pin set to semantic tag "vnext" which maps to multiple versions across regions. Resolver prefers highest semver available per region, uses capacity score to pick. If mismatch in compat-tags across regions, record per-region selected build in rollout metadata.

Rollout checklist for changes to pin-resolution logic:
- Add feature flag gate on control-plane resolver.
- Unit tests for decision flow branches (compat, capacity, region, tie-breaker).
- Backfill provenance store for last 30 days prior to flip (sampling ok).
- Canary run: 1% traffic for 48h, monitor pin_fallback_rate and error-trace volume.
- SRE playbook updated with new error strings and runbook ids.

Open questions / trade-offs (items for architecture review):
- Should the provenance blob be fully queryable (indexed) or archived and referenced by digest? Indexing increases storage cost but speeds investigations.
- How aggressive should precompute of compatibility indices be? Precompute reduces runtime work but is heavy at model churn.
- Tie-breakers: allow admin override (manual "pin-lock")? This adds complexity to rollback flows.
- What is the acceptable window for honor-pin-soft before falling back (5s? 50ms?). Need real perf numbers from serving runtime.

Immediate next steps / action items:
- (Sana) draft a small RFC describing the provenance schema and retention (due 2024-11-20).
- (Luca) prototype cache-key layout and TTL rules for resolution cache (POC by 2024-11-27).
- (Evelyn) wire basic fallback metrics into existing telemetry pipeline (INF-metrics) and add a dashboard stub.
- (Rohit) implement a sample log line and store in routes.fallbacks (PR target 2024-12-08).

Notes / scraps (working thoughts):
- Keep provenance compact — full registry snapshots per-request is too noisy. Use digest->blob approach.
- Consider recording per-rollout "binding manifest" to speed multi-region resolution for canaries.
- If we go to strict honor-pin as default later, need a migration path and UI hints in Console.

References / links to existing patterns:
- Registry design notes (confluence link above)
- Past incident: region-fallback-2024-07 (postmortem id: PM-2024-07-22-routing)

End of draft.

-- Sana
